findings.body: The Windows leak check treats a zero exit time from GetProcessTimes as proof that the process is running. Microsoft documents that the exit-time field is undefined until the process exits (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-getprocesstimes). If it is nonzero for a live launcher, `_running` returns false and `test_4_turn_log` passes despite the process being left behind. This weakens the test's process-leak assertion. Use a defined liveness check, such as WaitForSingleObject with a zero timeout, and verify that a live launcher makes the assertion fail.
